questions.question: D1 — Which implementation approach should these tests follow? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-approach>

options.label: B: Two tests + assertion hardening (Recommended)
options.description: Happy path + 502 tests using existing factory/mock/sleeper, with explicit assertions on Stripe call count, exact backoff sequence, and receipt fields. Turns tests into contracts, not vibe checks. Completeness: 8/10. Effort: human ~1.5 hrs / CC ~45 min.

options.label: A: Exactly the two tests as written
options.description: Happy path and 502 retry-exhaustion, minimal scope. Good enough, but assertions may remain vague (e.g. 'correct receipt' without field-level verification). Completeness: 6/10. Effort: human ~1 hr / CC ~30 min.

options.label: C: Parametric/table-driven test matrix
options.description: Wrap both cases in a table-driven structure. Scales well but adds abstraction overhead for just two cases (YAGNI risk). Completeness: 8/10. Effort: human ~2-3 hrs / CC ~1 hr.

questions.question: D2 — How should I approach the review of this test plan? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-mode>

options.label: HOLD SCOPE — maximum rigor (Recommended)
options.description: The two-test scope is right. Review for correctness, assertion completeness, edge cases, failure modes, and test isolation. Make it bulletproof. No expansions surfaced. Right call for a targeted test-coverage plan.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION — hold scope but show options
options.description: Review the two-test plan rigorously AND surface adjacent test opportunities (e.g. 429 retry path, receipt field-format variants, idempotency) as individual cherry-pick decisions. Neutral posture on each expansion.

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION — find the minimum
options.description: Challenge whether both tests are needed now or one can be deferred. Ruthless minimum. Usually right for a hotfix; probably overkill here.

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION — think bigger
options.description: Treat this as an opportunity to design the full test pyramid for processPayment(). Dream state: complete path coverage across all Stripe response codes, receipt formats, concurrency. Right when you want to build the cathedral now.

questions.question: D3 — Section 2 finding: the 502 exhaustion test needs a concrete failure contract. What does processPayment() do when retries are exhausted? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-502-failure-contract>

options.label: Raises a specific exception (Recommended)
options.description: processPayment() raises a named exception class (e.g. PaymentGatewayError, StripeChargeError) when retries are exhausted. The test asserts that exact exception is raised and that no receipt is generated. Plan should name the class. Most common in Ruby/Python codebases.

options.label: Returns a failure Result/Error object
options.description: processPayment() returns a Result or Response object with a success flag or error code (e.g. Result(ok: false, error: :gateway_unavailable)). The test asserts the error field value and that no receipt is in the return. Common in functional or Rust-influenced patterns.

options.label: Leave as-is — let implementer decide
options.description: Keep 'fails clean' as the stated outcome and let the implementer pick the assertion form. Defers the decision; risks an under-specified test that passes on wrong behavior (e.g. returns nil but no assertion on why).

questions.question: D4 — Section 5/6 finding: 'assert correct receipt is generated' is under-specified for Approach B. The test needs to assert specific receipt fields. How should the plan specify the receipt assertions? <gstack-qid:plan-ceo-receipt-assertion-spec>

options.label: Name key receipt fields in the plan (Recommended)
options.description: The plan lists the fields the test must assert: at minimum stripe_charge_id, amount, and currency. Any field whose value the test can know from the mock input is asserted explicitly. This turns 'correct receipt' into a verifiable contract. Implementer looks up exact field names from the Receipt class.

options.label: Assert non-nil receipt with no zero/nil fields
options.description: The test asserts that a receipt was returned and that its required fields are all present (non-nil, non-zero). Less precise than field-value matching, but catches the case where the receipt builder returns a blank receipt or nil.

options.label: Leave as 'correct receipt generated' — implementer decides
options.description: Keep the vague assertion. Risks a test that passes even if the wrong charge amount is in the receipt. Acceptable only if the receipt builder already has its own unit tests that verify field values (the plan says it does, but that's the builder, not the processPayment integration).

report:
# Payment Processing — Test Coverage

## Context

`processPayment()` has zero unit tests on its two most critical paths: success
(correctness) and 502 retry-exhaustion (graceful degradation). A broken happy
path or a retry that loops forever or that panics instead of failing cleanly
are both silent production incidents under the current coverage. This plan adds
exactly two unit tests to close that gap, using the existing test factory,
Stripe mock, and virtual sleeper already in place. Production code is not
touched.

Review mode: **HOLD SCOPE**. Approach: **B — assertion hardening** (explicit
call count, specific receipt fields, named exception on failure). Approved via
D1/D2 before review sections began.

---

## Scope

### Two unit tests for `processPayment()`

**Test 1 — Happy path**

Setup:
- `payment_test_factory(max_retries=1)` with Stripe mock configured to return
  HTTP 200 on the charge call.

Assertions (Approach B — field-level, not presence-only):
- Receipt is returned (non-nil).
- `stripe_charge_id` matches the mock charge ID.
- `amount` matches the input charge amount.
- `currency` matches the input currency.
- Stripe mock was called exactly **1 time** (no spurious retries on success).

> Implementer: look up exact field names from the `Receipt` class before
> writing assertions. The three fields above are the minimum; assert any
> additional fields whose values are deterministic from the mock inputs.

**Test 2 — 502 exhaustion path**

Setup:
- `payment_test_factory(max_retries=1)` with Stripe mock configured to return
  HTTP 502 on **every** call.
- Virtual sleeper injected (records backoff without real delays).

Assertions (Approach B):
- `processPayment()` raises a named exception (look up the exact class in the
  production code — e.g. `PaymentGatewayError` or `StripeChargeError`). The
  plan must name this class before implementation begins.
- **No receipt is generated** on this path (anti-assertion: exception raised
  means no receipt returned).
- Stripe mock was called exactly **2 times** (initial attempt + exactly one
  retry; `max_retries=1` enforced by the factory).
- Virtual sleeper recorded **1 backoff event** between the two charge attempts.

### Existing infrastructure retained

The following are reused as-is:
- `payment_test_factory` (configures `max_retries=1`, exposes mock call
  history)
- Stripe mock (records call history)
- Virtual sleeper (records backoff sequence; no real delays)
- Stripe adapter regression suite (network timeouts, 402 declines, 429 rate
  limits, 502→200 recovery) — unchanged
- Receipt-builder regression tests — unchanged

---

## Architecture

```
PRODUCTION (unchanged):
  processPayment()
    ├── Stripe HTTP client  [charge → 200 OK | 402 | 429 | 502]
    └── Receipt builder     [build receipt from charge_response]

NEW UNIT TESTS:
  Test 1 (happy path)
    payment_test_factory(max_retries=1)
      └── Stripe mock (returns 200) ──→ processPayment()
          assert: receipt.stripe_charge_id ✓
                  receipt.amount ✓
                  receipt.currency ✓
                  mock.call_count == 1 ✓

  Test 2 (502 exhaustion)
    payment_test_factory(max_retries=1)
      └── Stripe mock (returns 502 × 2) ──→ processPayment()
          virtual_sleeper records 1 backoff event
          assert: raises NamedExceptionClass ✓
                  no receipt returned ✓
                  mock.call_count == 2 ✓
                  virtual_sleeper.events.count == 1 ✓

Data flow — 502 path:
  charge_args ──▶ processPayment() ──▶ Stripe mock (502)
                                          │
                                 virtual_sleeper.record_backoff()
                                          │
                               retry ──▶ Stripe mock (502)
                                          │
                               raises NamedExceptionClass
                               (no receipt generated)
```

---

## NOT in scope

- `processPayment()` production code changes — explicitly excluded.
- Additional error code paths (402 decline, 429 rate limit, 503, 504, 0/timeout)
  as unit tests for `processPayment()` — covered at the adapter level; deferred
  from this plan.
- Parametric/table-driven test structure — YAGNI for two cases; consider when
  adding a 3rd path.
- Idempotency testing — separate concern; no infrastructure for it yet.
- Receipt field-value tests for every possible field — three key fields minimum;
  implementer adds more if deterministic from mock inputs.

## What already exists

| Existing piece | Solves which sub-problem | Reused? |
|----------------|--------------------------|---------|
| `payment_test_factory` | Stripe mock wiring, `max_retries=1`, call history | ✓ yes |
| Virtual sleeper | Backoff recording without real delays | ✓ yes |
| Stripe mock (call history API) | Asserting exact call count | ✓ yes |
| Stripe adapter suite (502→200 recovery) | Partial coverage of the retry path | ✓ retained (not replaced) |
| Receipt-builder regression tests | Receipt field correctness | ✓ retained (not replaced) |

## Dream state delta

```
CURRENT STATE                  THIS PLAN               12-MONTH IDEAL
No unit tests on               Two unit tests:         Full path coverage:
processPayment().              happy + 502 exhaustion  happy, 402, 429, 503,
Stripe adapter suite           with assertion          504, 0/timeout, partial
covers adapter-level           hardening (call count,  charges, idempotency,
edge cases only.               receipt fields,         concurrency. Test
processPayment()'s own         named exception).       pyramid complete.
contract is untested.
```

---

## Error & Rescue Registry

| Method / Codepath | What can go wrong | Exception class | Rescued? | Rescue action | User sees (test asserts) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| processPayment() — happy | Stripe returns 200 | N/A | N/A | — | receipt with correct fields |
| processPayment() — attempt 1 | Stripe returns 502 | NamedExceptionClass (TBD) | Y | backoff, retry | nothing yet |
| processPayment() — attempt 2 (retry) | Stripe returns 502 | NamedExceptionClass (TBD) | Y | retry exhausted → raise | exception raised; no receipt |

> **Action required before implementation:** identify the exact exception class
> raised by `processPayment()` on 502 retry exhaustion (approved D3). Update
> the plan with the class name before writing the test.

## Failure Modes Registry

| Codepath | Failure mode | Rescued? | Tested? | User sees | Logged? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| processPayment() happy | Stripe 200, receipt built | N/A | ✓ (Test 1) | correct receipt | N/A |
| processPayment() 502 (attempt 1) | Stripe 502 | Y | ✓ (Test 2) | nothing (transparent retry) | implied |
| processPayment() 502 (attempt 2) | Retry exhausted | Y (raises) | ✓ (Test 2) | named exception | implied |
| Receipt builder fails | BuildError | handled separately | ✓ (existing regression) | — | existing |

No CRITICAL GAPSs remaining after D3 and D4 approvals.

---

## Implementation Tasks

Synthesized from this review's findings. Run with Claude Code; checkbox as you ship.

- [ ] **T1 (P1, human: ~30min / CC: ~5min)** — processPayment() test — Specify and assert the named exception class on 502 retry exhaustion
  - Surfaced by: Section 2 Error & Rescue Map — "fails clean" was undefined; D3 approved raising a named exception
  - Files: `payment_test.rb` (or equivalent)
  - Verify: Test passes with the exception assertion; fails if you remove the retry or change the exception class

- [ ] **T2 (P1, human: ~20min / CC: ~5min)** — processPayment() test — Assert specific receipt fields in happy path test
  - Surfaced by: Section 5/6 Code Quality / Test Review — "correct receipt is generated" was vague; D4 approved field-level assertions
  - Files: `payment_test.rb`
  - Verify: Test passes with correct mock; fails if amount or stripe_charge_id are wrong

- [ ] **T3 (P1, human: ~10min / CC: ~2min)** — processPayment() test — Add anti-assertion confirming no receipt is generated on 502 exhaustion
  - Surfaced by: Section 6 Test Review — 502 path must confirm exception path does not accidentally return a receipt
  - Files: `payment_test.rb`
  - Verify: Test would fail if processPayment() returned a receipt alongside the exception
